note: j sounds like English y: jau5 rhymes with 'how' after a y.
z is like the ds in 'beds', with no puff of air. c (as in 草 cou2) has the puff.
c is like the ts in 'cats', with a puff of air: cou2. Compare 早 zou2, no puff.
ng- at the start, like the ng of 'singer'. Many young speakers say o5; learn ngo5.
aa is long, as in 'father'. 心 sam1 (heart) has the short a.
Short a, like the u in 'sum': sam1. Compare 三 saam1, with a long aa.
Final p: close your lips and stop. No puff, no extra vowel.
Final t: touch the tongue behind your teeth and stop without releasing it: cat1.
Final k: stop at the back of the mouth, with no puff: luk6.
b has no puff of air, closer to the p in 'spin' than to English b.
p has a strong puff of air, like the p in 'pin'. 婆婆 is grandma (mother's mother).
d has no puff, like the t in 'stop'. t (睇 tai2, to look) has the puff.
gw is one sound, a g with rounded lips: gwai3.
eo is one rounded vowel, a little like the u in 'fur' with rounded lips: heoi3.
oe is like the e in 'her' said with rounded lips: hoe1.
yu is 'ee' said with rounded lips, like German ü: syu1. Not 'syoo'.
Syllabic m: hum with closed lips on a low falling tone, m4. Not 'um'.
Syllabic ng: hum through the nose with the back of the tongue raised, ng5. Many people say m5.
Tone 1: high and level. Its twins: 史 si2, 試 si3, 時 si4, 市 si5, 事 si6.
Tone 2: starts in the middle and rises, like a surprised 'huh?'.
Tone 3: mid and level, like speaking calmly.
Tone 4: low and falling, the lowest tone.
Tone 5: starts low and rises a little. Less of a rise than tone 2 (史 si2).
Tone 6: low and level. 有事 = something's up; 冇事 = I'm fine.
Tone 5: low, rising a little. Say it with tone 6 and you get 賣 (to sell).
Tone 6: low and level. Mix up 買 and 賣 and you swap buyer and seller.
Tone 6: low and level, hai6. Its twin 喺 hai2 (at, in) rises.
Tone 2: rising, hai2. Say it low and level and you get 係 hai6 (to be).
Tone 3: mid and level, sei3. With tone 2 (sei2) it becomes 死, to die.
Tone 2: rising, sei2. This is why 4 is an unlucky number in Hong Kong.
Tone 2: rising, gau2. Its twins: 夠 gau3 (enough), 舊 gau6 (old).
Tone 3: mid and level, gau3. 夠喇 = that's enough.
Tone 6: low and level, gau6. For people, old is 老.
Tone 2: rising, fan2. Its twin 瞓 fan3 (to sleep) is mid and level.
Tone 3: mid and level, fan3. 瞓覺 = to go to sleep.
Tone 5: low rising, maa5. 媽 maa1 (mom) is tone 1, 麻 maa4 (numb) is tone 4.
Two legs walking.
As a radical on the left it often marks a spoken-Cantonese word: 嘅 咗 啲 嘢 呢.
Once a circle with a dot. 今日 = today.
A crescent moon. 一月 = January, 一個月 = one month.
日 (sun) + 月 (moon).
Three peaks. 山頂 is the Peak on Hong Kong Island.
A stream with drops on both sides.
A tree with branches and roots.
Two trees. Also a common family name, Lam.
人 (person) + 木 (tree): a person leaning on a tree. 休息 = to rest.
A person with arms stretched wide.
Little dots: the opposite of 大.
Two swinging doors, like a saloon. 門口 = doorway, entrance.
A hand with its fingers. 手機 = cell phone.
女 (woman) + 子 (child). Also 'very': 好平 (very cheap).
口 + 既: a spoken-Cantonese character. 我嘅 = my, mine.
口 + 左: 食咗 = have eaten. Never written in formal Chinese.
口 + 野: 買嘢 = to buy things, 食嘢 = to eat something.
Until about noon. There is no everyday 'good afternoon'.
For a service or a small favor, and to call a server. Literally 'it shouldn't be'.

meaning: Thank you! (for a gift or kind words)
note: For gifts, money and compliments. To a server, say 唔該.
Bumping into someone, being late. A real apology is 對唔住.
From English 'bye-bye', the usual goodbye. 再見 is more formal.
For strangers and first meetings. With friends it sounds stiff: say their name or 早晨.
晒 makes it stronger. For help with directions, a door held open, a favor.

meaning: Thank you so much! (for a gift)
note: Warmer than 多謝 alone, for a present or a treat.
Literally 'no need to be polite'. Also just 唔使.
A real apology, when you were in the wrong.
The usual answer to 唔好意思 or 對唔住.
Many people just say OK here.
Said to someone going to bed, or at the end of a late chat.
Literally 'very long, not seen'.
快樂 = happy. For the Lunar New Year, say 恭喜發財 or 新年快樂.
請 invites: 請坐, 請入嚟 (please come in). It is not a general 'please'.
Only for answering the phone or calling out to someone.
Literally 'wishing you wealth'. You can answer with the same words.
哋 makes a pronoun plural: 我哋 (we), 你哋 (you all).
我 + 哋. There is one word for 'we', whether or not it includes the listener.
The second syllable rises to tone 1: maa4 maa1.
Like 媽媽, the second syllable rises: baa4 baa1.
There is no plain 'brother': younger brother is 細佬.
There is no plain 'sister': younger sister is 細妹.
Older brother: 哥哥. 細佬 is also 'little brother' in general.
Older sister: 家姐.
Your mother's father is 公公.
Your mother's mother is 婆婆.
Your father's father is 爺爺.
Your father's mother is 嫲嫲.
The everyday word. 老婆 is wife.
Everyday and affectionate, not rude as 'old woman' might sound.
Literally 'the boy'. Daughter: 個女. 我個仔 = my son.
我朋友 (my friend): no 嘅 needed with close people.
佢 is he, she or it: the context tells you which.

meaning: There are four people in my family.
note: 屋企 = home, family. People take the classifier 個.
叫 = to be called.
The question word sits where the answer goes: 我叫安娜.
姓 = to have the family name. The family name comes first: 陳大文.
阿 + a name is the friendly form. Many Hong Kong people also use an English name.
Literally 'you are a where person?'. Answer: 我係美國人.
Country + 人 (person): 香港人, 中國人.
加拿大 = Canada. No word for 'a': 我係 + nationality.
三藩市 is the name Cantonese speakers use; 舊金山 is also heard.
No word for 'a' before a job: 我係老師, 我係醫生.
No 係 before an age. 今年 = this year.

meaning: I can speak a little Cantonese.
note: 識 = know how to. 少少 = a little.
緊 after the verb: in the middle of doing it.
同 joins two nouns: 英文同廣東話.
普通話 is Mandarin. Cantonese is 廣東話.
Where comes before the verb: 喺屋企 + 講.
鍾意 + verb = like doing. 睇戲 = to see a movie.
Read phone numbers digit by digit. Hong Kong numbers have eight digits.
兩 before a classifier, never 二: 兩個人, 兩杯茶.
Ten + five. Fifty is 五十.
In speech, twenty-something is often 廿: 廿五 (25).
廿 (jaa6) is a short way to say 二十 in numbers from 21 to 29.
Four tens and eight: no extra word for 'and'.
Nine tens + nine: 九十九.
Short for 一百五十. 105 is 一百零五.
零 (zero) marks the empty tens place.
One thousand: 一千. Two thousand is 兩千 or 二千.
2,000 is 兩千 or 二千, both common; 二 always stays in 二十 and 十二.
Cantonese counts in 萬 (10,000): 100,000 is 十萬.
A hundred 萬: 100 × 10,000.
In phone numbers, say 零 for each 0.
蚊 = dollar in speech: 五十蚊, 一百蚊.
蚊 is 'dollar' in speech; 元 is the written word on price tags.
半 = half, so half a dollar after 蚊.
毫子 = ten cents: 五毫子 is five ten-cent units.
Written HK$ or HKD. Money in speech: 蚊.
個 is the general classifier, but many nouns have their own.
本 for books and magazines. Not 三書.
呢 + classifier + noun: never 呢書.
邊 + classifier asks 'which'.
A classifier with no number in front means 'the': 本書.
張 for flat things: tickets, tables, photos, paper. 飛 is 'ticket' (from English 'fare').
張 again: tables are flat. 枱 is also a desk.
隻 for most animals, and for one of a pair (一隻鞋).
兩 + 隻 + 狗. 二隻 is wrong.
Owner + classifier + noun means 'my': no 嘅 needed.
架 for cars, planes and bikes.

meaning: a top; a piece of clothing
note: 件 for shirts, jackets and most clothes.
條 for long, thin things: pants, roads, fish. One 條, not 'a pair'.
對 = pair. One shoe is 一隻鞋.
杯 for a cup or glass of a drink. Not 一個水.
碗 = bowl, used as the classifier.
嗰 = that: 嗰 + classifier + noun.
幾 + classifier asks how many, for small numbers.
Literally 'drink tea': a dim sum meal with tea.
The small dishes themselves. 飲茶 is the meal.
A dim sum classic: 一籠蝦餃 (a steamer of shrimp dumplings).
The open dumplings with a yellow wrapper. 賣 rises here: siu1 maai2.
叉燒 = Cantonese barbecue pork, 包 = bun.
Soft rolls with shrimp or barbecue pork, in sweet soy sauce.
A Hong Kong bakery favorite.
No pineapple inside: the crackly top looks like one.
碗 for a bowl. Wontons with shrimp in a light broth.
Hong Kong milk tea, strong and creamy. Hot: 熱奶茶.
The cha chaan teng classic. Stir to crush the lemon.
Coffee and milk tea mixed. Named after a pair of mandarin ducks.
唔該 + 我要 + number + classifier + drink.
走 = leave out. Less sweet: 少甜.
What staff ask at the door. 位 is the polite classifier for people. Answer: 兩位.
定 = or, in questions. 外賣 = takeout.

meaning: Why don't we go for dim sum?
note: 不如 suggests; 吖 makes it a friendly invitation.
Say it to any server, or draw a little circle in the air.
呀 makes it friendly. Answer: 三十蚊.

meaning: Could you make it a bit cheaper?
note: Fine at markets, not in malls or chain stores.

meaning: Do you have it in a large?
note: Sizes: 細碼, 中碼, 大碼.
先 at the end: 'first', i.e. for now.

meaning: Can I pay with an Octopus card?
note: 八達通: the transit card that also pays in shops.
件 is the classifier for clothes on the upper body: 一件衫, 呢件外套.
太 = too. 喇 marks a new situation: 'now it's too much'.
Talking about clothes, so the classifier 件 stands in for the noun.
嗰 = that, 呢 = this. 睇吓 = have a look.
試吓 = give it a try. Works for clothes, shoes and food samples.

meaning: Do you have it in another color?
note: 第二 here means 'another', not 'second'. 隻 is the classifier for colors: 呢隻色.
啱 = right, fitting. Too big: 太大喇. Too small: 太細喇.
細 = small. The opposite is 大.
收 = accept. Small shops and market stalls often take only cash or Octopus.
畀 = give, pay. Many people just say 'cash' in English here.
散紙 = coins and small bills. 冇 = don't have.
Hong Kong charges for plastic bags, so you will often be asked 使唔使袋呀？

meaning: I'd like to buy a present.
note: 份 is the classifier for gifts and newspapers.
Time words go before the verb: 我聽日去.
星期 + number; Sunday is 星期日. 禮拜一 means the same.
點 = o'clock: 三點 (three o'clock).
半 = half.
Month first, then day: big to small.
幾 asks 'which number': the answer is 星期五, 星期六 and so on.
Some people say 尋日 instead. Today is 今日.
Hour + 點, then minutes + 分. Many people count in fives: 三點兩個字 is also 3:10.
Hong Kong speech uses the 12-hour clock: 朝早 (morning), 下晝 (afternoon), 夜晚 (evening) go first.

meaning: I get up at seven in the morning.
note: Who, then when, then the verb: the time goes before 起身.

meaning: What time do you start work?
note: 幾點 sits before the verb, where the answer will go: 我九點返工.

meaning: I get off work at six.
note: 放工 = finish work; 返工 = go to work.
食晏 = have lunch. 晏 also means late: 晏啲 (a bit later).
沖涼 = take a shower. Many people in Hong Kong shower at night.

meaning: I go to bed at eleven.
note: 瞓覺 = sleep, go to bed.

meaning: What do you do on weekends?
note: 週末 = weekend. Saturday and Sunday: 星期六日.
Literally 'your birthday is which month, which day?'

Thing + 喺 + 邊度. 廁所 is more direct.
行 here is haang4 (walk).
Right: 轉右.

meaning: The bank is next to the supermarket.
note: The place word comes after its noun: 超市隔籬.

meaning: Is there an MTR station nearby?
note: Place first, then 有: 'nearby has…'.

meaning: Excuse me, how do I get to the MTR station?
note: 請問 = may I ask. 點去 = how to go.
過 = go across. 馬路 = road (literally 'horse road').
Noun first, then the place word: 銀行對面, not 對面銀行.
喺 (hai2, tone 2) is 'at, in'. 係 (hai6, tone 6) is 'to be'.
Literally 'walk five minutes and you're there'. 就 = then, right away.
Verb-not-verb question: answer 遠 or 唔遠.
好 here means 'very', not 'good'.
前面 = in front; 後面 = behind.

meaning: Turn right at the traffic lights.
note: Where you turn goes before the verb: 喺紅綠燈 + 轉右.

meaning: The park is on the left.
note: 左邊 = left side; 右邊 = right side.

meaning: The bookstore is inside the mall.
note: 入面 = inside, after its noun: 商場入面.
Ask it when you are lost. Here 係 links two places, so it is 係, not 喺.
The usual question on the phone.
Most people just say 地鐵.
Tap it on the MTR, buses, ferries and in shops.
To a taxi driver. You can call him 師傅.
Shout it on a minibus so the driver stops.

meaning: I take the MTR to work.
note: How you travel goes before the verb: 搭地鐵 + 返工.

meaning: I take the bus to Central.
note: 坐 and 搭 both work for buses. Not 我去中環坐巴士, which means 'I go to Central to take a bus'.
的士 comes from English 'taxi'. 吖 makes it a suggestion.

meaning: Does this minibus go to Mong Kok?
note: 架 is the classifier for vehicles. Ask the driver before you get on.
落車 = get off; 上車 = get on.
The green and white ferry across Victoria Harbour. Pay with Octopus.

meaning: I'm on the MTR right now.
note: 緊 after the verb: the action is going on now.

meaning: Have you ever been to Macau?
note: 過 = have ever done; 未 at the end asks 'yet?'.
未 + verb + 過: not yet, never so far.
行路 = walk. 行 here is haang4.
下個 = next; 上個 = last.

meaning: How long does it take to get to Tsim Sha Tsui by MTR?
note: 幾耐 = how long. Answer: 十分鐘.

meaning: When are you coming to Hong Kong?
note: 嚟 = come (toward the speaker); 去 = go.
返 = go back: 返屋企 (go home).
Also how you address a teacher: 陳老師, or just 老師.
University student: 大學生.
返 = go back: 返工, 返學, 返屋企.

meaning: What line of work are you in?
note: 行 here is hong4 (trade). 㗎 makes it a friendly question.
Where you work goes before the verb: 喺銀行 + 做嘢.
識 = know how to. Answer 識 or 唔識, not 'yes'.
想 = want to, would like to.
唔識 = don't know how. Not 我唔可以寫, which means 'I'm not allowed to write'.
要 = have to. Time goes before the verb.
可以 = allowed to, possible. For a skill you learned, use 識.

meaning: I don't have to work today.
note: 唔使 = no need to.

meaning: I'll be a bit late tomorrow.
note: 會 = will (likely). 遲啲 = a bit late.
係 joins two nouns: I = a student.
No 嘅 needed with people close to you: 我同事, 我朋友.
開會 = hold or attend a meeting.

meaning: I have an exam next week.
note: 下個禮拜 = next week; 上個禮拜 = last week.
讀書 = study, go to school. 喺邊度 goes before the verb.
鍾意 + verb = like doing something.
Where does it hurt? 你邊度唔舒服呀？
Body part + 痛: 肚痛 (stomachache), 牙痛 (toothache).
咗 shows the change has happened.
藥 = medicine.
For emergencies. For everyday help: 可唔可以幫吓我呀？
有啲 = a little, somewhat.
喉嚨 = throat. Same pattern: body part + 痛.

meaning: I need to see a doctor.
note: 睇醫生 = see a doctor (literally 'look at a doctor').
Medicine is 'eaten' in Cantonese: 食藥.

meaning: I haven't taken my medicine yet.
note: 未 = not yet. 冇 would mean 'I didn't'.
Literally 'I have no matter'. Also 'It's nothing'.
吓 after the verb makes the request lighter.
For emergencies: 急症室 is the emergency room.
Also 'Watch out!'
Said to someone who is sick.

meaning: I've been coughing for a few days.
note: 咳 = cough. 幾日 = a few days.
999 is Hong Kong's emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.
病咗 = has fallen ill. For 'I feel unwell', say 我唔舒服.
靚 is pretty, good-looking, or just good (靚衫, nice clothes).
No 係 before an adjective: 呢件衫好平.
好食 = good to eat; the first 好 means 'very'.
Adjective + 過 + the other person.
好 is often just glue, not a strong 'very'.
太 = too. 辣 = spicy.
幾 before an adjective = quite.
A polite way to say something is bad.
Neither good nor bad.
The describer with 嘅 goes before the noun.
嘈 = noisy. Quiet: 靜.
Literally 'Hong Kong, very many people': no verb needed.
叻 = clever, good at things. A common compliment.
Adjective + 啲 = a bit more: 平啲, 大啲, 快啲.

meaning: The MTR is faster than the bus.
note: Adjective + 過 + what you compare with. No word for 'more' is needed.

meaning: The Octopus card is really handy.
note: 方便 = convenient.

meaning: The weather is really nice today.
note: 好好: the first 好 is 'very', the second 'good'.
後生 = young. Old: 老.
In a sentence it stays where the answer goes: 你食咩呀？
Also 'which one' before a noun: 邊個人.
呢 asks the same question back.
吖 makes it an invitation.
㗎 asserts or explains: 'it really is so'.
In a sentence: 你點解唔去呀？ (Why aren't you going?)
In a sentence it goes before the verb: 你幾時去呀？
Verb-not-verb question. Answer 係 or 唔係.
Answer with the verb: 去 (yes) or 唔去 (no).
Ask it after a suggestion. Answer 好 or 唔好.
啦 here agrees. Also 好吖 when you accept an invitation.
啦 urges. 快啲 = a bit faster.
咩 at the end shows surprise.

meaning: What do you want to eat?
note: The question word stays at the end, where the answer goes: 我想食麵.
佢 is he or she: the context tells you which.
有冇 = have or not have. Answer 有 or 冇.
點 before the verb asks how: answer 我搭地鐵返屋企.
啦 softens a request you have just made.
Not 我係攰: adjectives take 好, not 係.
冇 = not have. Never 唔有.
冇 + verb for what did not happen; not 我唔去咗.
兩 before a classifier, never 二個人.
A friendly hello around mealtimes, not an invitation.
Not 佢係高. 好 here is barely 'very'.
No 係 with ages: not 我係三十歲.
未 = not yet. 我冇食 means 'I didn't eat'.
過 = have been, not 'went'. For 'I went last week', use 咗.
冇 is the only negative of 有.
People say 我幾好 or 我好好; a bare 我好 is less usual, since 好 also means 'very'.
No 咗 for how you felt then: 琴日 already says when. (我攰咗 means 'I've gotten tired'.)
好 before an adjective means 'very', not 'good'.
Literally 'ghost guy'. Common among friends but can offend: learn it, don't use it.
多謝 for gifts and kindness; 唔該 for a service.

meaning: I used to eat dim sum all the time.
note: No 咗 for habits: 以前 already shows it is the past.
唔係 before a noun; plain 唔 before an adjective: 唔貴.
返 literally 'go back', but 返學 just means go to school.
有冇時間？ = do you have time? 時候 is "the time when".
冇錢 = to have no money. Never 唔有錢.
返屋企 = go home. No 嘅 needed: 我屋企.
Spoken: 份工 is more common. 做嘢 = to work.
呢個地方 = this place. Classifier 個.
冇問題 = no problem. Classifier 個 or 條.
咩意思呀？ = what does it mean?
你叫咩名呀？ Said meng2 in speech.
中文字 = Chinese characters.
打電話 = to make a call. Changed tone: waa2.
Classifier 部: 我部手機.
Classifier 部.
睇電視 = to watch TV.
In speech people often say 戲: 睇戲.
Classifier 件: 一件衫.
Classifier 對: 一對鞋.
Classifier 架: 一架車. 揸車 = to drive.
From English bus. 搭巴士 = to take the bus.
From English taxi. 搭的士.
搭地鐵 = take the MTR.
搭飛機 = to fly.
行街 = to go out shopping.
過馬路 = to cross the road.

Classifier 間: 一間學校.

返公司 = to go to the office.
Classifier 間.
Classifier 間.

Not a bar: 酒店 is a hotel.
去公園行吓 = go for a walk in the park.
去機場 = to the airport.
Polite word. 廁所 is plainer.

Classifier 張: 一張床.
Classifier 張: 一張枱.
Classifier 張.

開燈 / 閂燈 = lights on / off.
開冷氣 = turn on the A/C.

一杯咖啡.
牛肉, 豬肉 = beef, pork.

Classifier 條.
Hong Kong word; written 水果.
食早餐.
食晚飯.
今日天氣好好.
落雨 = to rain.
好大太陽 = very sunny.
Classifier 隻.
Classifier 隻.

女仔 is a girl or young woman.
女仔 for a girl.
男仔 for a boy.

meaning: little one (kind word for a child)
note: Also how adults speak to kids.

陳太 is short for 陳太太.
李小姐. Also to call a waitress.
Also how students address each other.
睇醫生 = to see a doctor.
Also used to call a shopkeeper.

隔籬鄰居 = next-door neighbor.
Neutral. 鬼佬 is slang.

睇地圖.
Classifier 部.
Classifier 本.
